chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and Fadala ibn Ayyub, all from al-Kinanī, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) mentioning Hajj,
so he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is one of the two Jihad, and it is the Jihad of the weak, and we are the weak.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Hajj as the Jihad of the weak in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes Hajj as the 'Jihad of the weak' (Jihad al-Du'afa), a concept central to Shia jurisprudence that elevates pilgrimage to the status of military struggle for those unable to fight. By linking this to the Prophet's statement, the Imam underscores the spiritual merit of Hajj as an accessible form of devotion for the broader community, reinforcing its status as one of the two primary forms of Jihad alongside armed struggle.
